Change 1687 pushed for review (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1687), commit 1dce563bcc.

Implemented: DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX 1800 -> 2400 (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh), the pinned test tightened from >= 1.0x to >= 2.0x DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS via a named DEFER_BOUND_REVIEW_CAP_MULTIPLE constant (test updated, not deleted), and the restated 1800s cadence figure in monitoring_autodeploy.tf corrected. Local gates: pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py 13 passed; terraform fmt -check + validate pass; make lint clean.

PROVENANCE NOTE, recorded so the decision is not later mistaken for a tracker-native one: the approval to raise the bound reached me through the operator dispatch, NOT as a written approval in the store. The lorikeet sweep (b902-18af-14ed-4da1 comment 12) recorded this as one of two items 'surfaced for operator decision'. It also runs AGAINST piranha's (7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9) closed disposition, which said 'I would not raise the bound' on the strength of a saturated-episode trace where in_flight oscillated 2 -> 1 -> 2 and never reached 0 for 30 minutes.

Both the code comment and the test docstring state that tension explicitly rather than papering over it: 2400s absorbs the four 10-130s overshoots the Aug-12 markers actually show, and does NOT fix a saturated episode, against which a larger bound only defers the same kill. Whether the Aug-12 episodes were saturated is unestablished -- comment 12 presents terminal markers only, no per-episode in_flight traces. The residual concurrency-gauge-vs-single-review-timer finding stays open on 7b4a's chain.

No operator apply needed for this ticket: the terraform edit is comment-only, so plan is a no-op.
